identity.name: Duchy of Parma and Piacenza
alt_names: Duchy of Parma, Piacenza and Guastalla

land.text: 'In 1814, the duchies were given to Napoleon's Habsburg wife, Marie-Louise'

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Restored: 11 April 1814'. The duchies had been annexed to France (first-french-empire records 1808). Marie Louise held them 'for the rest of her life'; the Final Act of 9 June 1815 gave Parma, Piacenza and Guastalla to her 'for her lifetime' (Congress of Vienna page).

land.text: 'In December 1859, the Duchy of Parma and Piacenza was combined with the Grand Duchy of Tuscany and the Duchy of Modena to form the United Provinces of Central Italy'

successors.note: Infobox 'Ceded to the United Provinces of Central Italy: 8 December 1859'; 'In March 1860, after a referendum, this merged with the Kingdom of Sardinia.'

capitals.name: Parma
capitals.note: The page text read does not print the capital field; Parma is the seat by the state's name and the gazetteer's core cell. Unverified: page output.

correction.text: the duchies of Parma, Piacenza and Guastalla as Marie Louise held them: Cliopatria's 1815 shape plus Guastalla, minus Pontremoli (a Tuscan enclave until 1847)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Parma shape begins in 1815 but the infobox gives 'Restored: 11 April 1814'. The shape is the 1815 outline with Guastalla added and Pontremoli removed (see the 1815 verdict).

correction.text: the duchies of Parma, Piacenza and Guastalla as Marie Louise held them: Cliopatria's 1815 shape plus Guastalla, minus Pontremoli (a Tuscan enclave until 1847)

keyframe_review.note: 7,460 km2 for 1815-1847, the same outline as 1849-1858: it carries Pontremoli (a Tuscan enclave until Marie Louise's death on 17 December 1847, when 'Tuscany agreed to transfer all its Lunigiana enclaves except Fivizzano' to Parma) and lacks Guastalla, which Parma held until the same day ('Parma, in turn, ceded the former Duchy of Guastalla to Modena'). Infobox area 5,660 km2 for 1852 (2,184 sq mi), ratio 1.32: within a factor of two, but the Cliopatria polygon is the larger.

7,460 km2 for 1849-1858: Parma and Piacenza with the Lunigiana enclaves of 1847 and without Guastalla, as the Treaty of Florence page describes the post-1847 duchy. Infobox 5,660 km2 in 1852: ratio 1.32, within a factor of two.
7,344 km2 for 1859, 1.6 percent below the 1849 shape, the same duchy; ends with its cession to the United Provinces of Central Italy on 8 December 1859 (infobox).

correction.text: the 1849 outline, for the year of the uprising

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Parma shape for 1848. The page says the Bourbon-Parma regime provoked 'an uprising in 1848 which temporarily drove them out', so the duchy continues in law; the shape is the 1849 outline.

region.text: the duchies of Parma, Piacenza and Guastalla as Marie Louise held them: Cliopatria's 1815 shape plus Guastalla, minus Pontremoli (a Tuscan enclave until 1847)

ledger.note: 11 April 1814: the duchies of Parma and Piacenza pass to Marie Louise. Infobox 'Restored: 11 April 1814'; 'In 1814, the duchies were given to Napoleon's Habsburg wife, Marie-Louise'. The page does not say when she took possession; the Final Act of 9 June 1815 confirmed Parma, Piacenza and Guastalla to her 'for her lifetime' (Congress of Vienna page).

17 December 1847: Parma cedes Guastalla to Modena. 'Parma, in turn, ceded the former Duchy of Guastalla to Modena'; the treaty took effect 'Upon the death of Marie Louise, Duchess of Parma, Piacenza, and Guastalla (occurred on 17 December 1847)'.

region.text: the Lunigiana enclaves of Tuscany, Pontremoli and Bagnone among them

ledger.note: 17 December 1847: Parma receives the Tuscan enclaves of Lunigiana. 'Tuscany agreed to transfer all its Lunigiana enclaves except Fivizzano'; the page names Pontremoli and Bagnone among the Tuscan enclaves ceded to Parma (paraphrase). grand-duchy-of-tuscany records the loss of Pontremoli in 1847.

17 December 1847: Marie Louise dies and the duchy passes from the Habsburg duchess to the Bourbon-Parma. 'After her death in 1847, the Duchy was restored to the Bourbon-Parma family, which had been ruling the tiny Duchy of Lucca'; the Treaty of Florence page dates her death 17 December 1847.

region.text: the duchy driven from its duke by the uprising

ledger.note: 1848: Parma leaves its duke and votes for union with Sardinia. Page silent: the Parma page says only that the Bourbon-Parma regime provoked 'an uprising in 1848 which temporarily drove them out'. The union vote is dated from kingdom-of-sardinia's dossier ('Spring 1848', its own page), not from a page opened here.

region.text: the duchy back under its duke

ledger.note: August 1848: Parma returns to its duke after the armistice of Salasco. Page silent: the Parma page says the dukes were only 'temporarily' driven out; the month is dated from kingdom-of-sardinia's dossier (its First Italian War of Independence page), not from a page opened here.

8 December 1859: Parma is ceded to the United Provinces of Central Italy. Infobox 'Ceded to the United Provinces of Central Italy: 8 December 1859'; 'The Bourbons ruled until 1859, when they were driven out by a revolution following the French and Sardinian victory.'

wars.name: Revolution of 1848 in Parma
wars.outcome: The Bourbon-Parma regime was 'temporarily' driven out by 'an uprising in 1848'; the dukes returned and no land changed hands on this page.
wars.note: The page gives no month; kingdom-of-sardinia's dossier has the spring 1848 vote and the August return.

wars.name: Second Italian War of Independence
wars.outcome: 'driven out by a revolution following the French and Sardinian victory' in 1859; Parma joined the United Provinces of Central Italy on 8 December 1859 and Sardinia in March 1860.
wars.note: Listed because it ended the state; the page does not place any fighting on the duchy's land.

certainty.note: Borders with Modena, Tuscany and Sardinia were fixed by the Final Act and the 1844 Treaty of Florence; Cliopatria's outline is coarse (about one H3 cell, 250 km2, of error).

notes: Written from the Parma article and the Treaty of Florence page (page budget 1-2); the Congress of Vienna page is cited in notes. Cliopatria's Parma outline is one polygon for 1815-1858 (7,460 km2): it holds Pontremoli from 1815 and no Guastalla, i.e. the post-1847 duchy; the corrections add Guastalla and remove Pontremoli before 17 December 1847 and the ledger reverses them on that day. The 1848 loss and gain are mirrors of kingdom-of-sardinia's ledger at confidence 1 (the Parma page does not mention the annexation vote or the Salasco armistice); the Cliopatria row has no 1848 shape (new keyframe). Not on the pages: Marie Louise's actual entry into Parma (1816), the dukes' names and reigns (no rulers list read, so none given), the 9 June 1859 flight of the regent, Austrian occupation. The capital field was not printed by the page text read. Gazetteer names needed: places Guastalla, Pontremoli, Bagnone. Cliopatria's infobox ratio 1.32 is within the factor of two.
